chunk_findings.detail: `close()` only sets `self.closed = True`; it leaves `self.connected` true. `_guarded()` gates calls on `connected`, not `closed`, so a closed client still answers. With `c = FakeMcpClient(); c.connect(1); c.close(); c.list_tools(1)`, the last call returns an OK outcome (tools/list) instead of `UNAVAILABLE`, so any test of post-close behavior or of the closed flag is wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/mcp.py:FakeMcpClient.close

chunk_findings.detail: `connect()` sets `self.connected = True` before checking `reply.status`. If the initialize reply is an error, the method returns a failed `Handshake` but leaves the client marked connected. For a stub server whose `handle` returns `W.err(msg["id"], W.INTERNAL_ERROR, "bad")` for `initialize` and a normal reply for `tools/list`, `c.connect(1)` returns status `ERROR`, yet `c.list_tools(1)` does not return `UNAVAILABLE` and proceeds to call the server. A failed handshake should leave the client disconnected.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/mcp.py:FakeMcpClient.connect

chunk_findings.detail: The constructor/docstring says `results` may map a tool name to “an Exception to raise”, but `handle()` only special-cases `W.ToolError`. Given `FakeMcpServer(tools=[{"name": "x"}], results={"x": RuntimeError("boom")})`, a `tools/call` for `x` returns `W.ok(mid, RuntimeError("boom"))` (a successful JSON-RPC result containing an exception object) instead of raising or returning an error. Thus scripted exception results do not exercise the error/`serve` exception path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/mcp.py:FakeMcpServer.handle

chunk_findings.detail: When `intercept(msg, self.notify)` returns `True`, `serve` executes `continue` before the `after()` block, so the documented contract that `after()` “runs once per message, answered or not” is violated. For example, `StdioServer(...).serve([{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "ping"}], intercept=lambda msg, notify: True, after=counter)` leaves the counter at `0` even though one message was processed by the interceptor; any caller using `after` for per-message bookkeeping or ratchets will undercount offloaded calls.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/mcp.py:StdioServer.serve

chunk_findings.detail: In the `OSError` branch, `connect` returns `Handshake(UNAVAILABLE, detail=...)` without passing the caller’s requested `version` into `protocol`. Thus `StdioClient(starter=raise OSError, argv=["x"]).connect(1.0, version="2024-11-05")` reports `handshake.protocol.offered == "2025-03-26"` (the default `OFFER_VERSION`) instead of `"2024-11-05"`, corrupting the protocol-version fact for an unavailable server.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/mcp.py:StdioClient.connect

chunk_findings.detail: `receive` appends each read chunk and immediately trims the accumulated buffer with `_keep` before checking for a newline. If the buffer is at or near `_MAX_BUF`, that trim can discard the newline that terminated a complete JSON-RPC line. For example, after `_MAX_BUF` bytes of an initialize response have been read without a newline, a subsequent `os.read` can return `\n` followed by another 64 KiB of data; `_keep` drops the first 64 KiB of the combined buffer, including that newline, so the reader never sees the line terminator and times out even though the server answered. The buffer should be split into lines first and only the remaining partial line trimmed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/companions/probe.py:_ProcessChannel.receive

chunk_findings.detail: The AST guard intended to forbid the default adapter from importing another ddflow layer misses relative imports. `ast.ImportFrom` stores the dotted path without leading dots and records relative depth in `level`; for example, `from ..services import probe` yields `module='services'` and `level=2`, and `from . import probe` yields `module=''`/`None`. The comprehension at line 194 produces `'services'` or `''`, which does not start with `ddflow` or `.` and is not `subprocess`, so the assertion passes. Thus adding a relative ddflow import such as `from ..services import probe` to `ddflow/adapters/mcp.py` would not be caught by this test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapters_mcp.py:199

chunk_findings.detail: `after()` is documented as running “once per message, answered or not,” but when `intercept(msg, self.notify)` returns True the loop `continue`s before the `after` call. A normal `tools/call` message that `intercept` takes over will therefore never run `after`. If the caller uses `after` to mark an offloaded call complete (which is the apparent purpose given `surfaces/mcp/_serve.py` was modified to add `intercept` and `after`), this leaves the call/state outstanding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/mcp.py:StdioServer.serve

chunk_findings.detail: After a successful JSON-RPC `initialize` response, `connect` sends `notifications/initialized` unconditionally. Given a server result of `{"protocolVersion": "2030-01-01"}` (outside `SERVED_VERSIONS`), `negotiate` correctly returns `supported=False`, but the client still sends `initialized` and reports `status == OK`. The adapter thereby continues the MCP initialization flow for a protocol revision it declares unsupported, letting a caller later use `list_tools`/`call` on a connection that failed version negotiation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/mcp.py:StdioClient.connect

chunk_findings.detail: The server does not enforce JSON-RPC request validity. A top-level JSON value that is not an object, e.g. the line `"not-a-frame"`, receives `-32602 INVALID_PARAMS`; JSON-RPC 2.0 specifies `-32600 Invalid Request`. Likewise `handle` accepts and executes requests missing `"jsonrpc": "2.0"`. This makes the wire adapter reject/accept invalid peers with the wrong wire-level semantics.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/mcp.py:StdioServer.serve, StdioServer.handle

chunk_findings.detail: The diff deletes `import json`, `_ECHO_MARK`, `_reply_to`, and `_describe_answer`, but leaves `verify_one` unchanged below the visible hunks. `verify_one` is the consumer of exactly those names for building and parsing the initialize request; a normal call such as `verify_one(c)` now raises `NameError` (`json` or `_reply_to`) instead of returning a `Verification`, so companion probing crashes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/companions/probe.py:verify_one

chunk_findings.detail: The AST scan fails to detect relative imports because `ast.ImportFrom` stores the leading dots in the `level` field, not in `module`. For example, `from . import registry` yields `module=None`, so the expression `(n.module or "")` becomes `""`; the assertion’s `m.startswith(".")` check is never triggered. As a result, a prohibited relative import inside `ddflow/adapters/mcp.py` would be silently accepted, defeating the test’s stated guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapters_mcp.py:test_the_default_adapter_imports_no_other_ddflow_layer_and_no_subprocess
